name: Rose Glass independent body response maps
source: Each body was rendered alone at the contact sheet's 0-second light setting, once over black and once over white. Its shadow was rendered separately over white. No signed scene delta is used in these maps.
coordinates: For a 9:16 output UV measured from top-left, material point p=(uv.x*720-65,uv.y*1280). Transform p through that body's inverse deformation before sampling the two response maps at ((p.x+65)/720,p.y/1280). Outside their 1080x1920 domain use the unchanged under-color, not clamp-to-edge texels. Pin upper-body deformation to zero across the first 155 material pixels from the top, and lower-body deformation across the last 155 from the bottom: their cropped ends have no atlas data beyond the frame.
composition: Begin with the scene background and process upper, lower, foreground in that order.
For each body, apply its shadow attenuation to the current under-color in linear light: under=toSrgb(toLinear(under)*toLinear(shadowSample)). The shadow sample is white outside the penumbra.

At that body's inverse-deformed reference coordinate sample blackSample B and whiteSample W. In sRGB, result=clamp(B+(W-B)*under,0,1). B is the body over black; W-B is its measured per-channel transmission of the underlayer.
Do not multiply B by an additional SVG alpha or clip it to the SVG edge. The rendered B/W maps already contain the soft optical boundary and return the under-color outside the body.

For the moving shadow, sample its own shadow map at an inverse-deformed point whose shadow offset follows the moved body. A separately shifted shadow point is preferable to reusing the exact surface point.

restingCheck.note: Independent response maps reproduce the static material approximately; the four signed PNGs remain the exact resting image. Keep both paths and compare the handoff at the first drag frame.

limitations: These are fixed-light appearance responses, not a full dynamic normal or thickness field. Add small Jacobian/normal-based light and absorption changes after sampling for pressure and stretch.

The upper and lower bodies are cropped by the source frame. Large unpinned movement at those cropped ends reveals a straight atlas boundary; taper displacement to zero toward the corresponding frame edge.
The original shadows depend on current shape and depth. A warped reference shadow is a starting point, not a substitute for validating newly exposed rear layers and contact/penumbra placement.
B/W response is approximately affine in sRGB; compare every dragged reference frame rather than inferring success from the 2.403 static error.
